lesson_title: Report Card Day: the Year-End Run
hook_text: A shop keeps a diary all year. Then one day the diary has to become a report card.
clip_script: All year, Zanele's shop has been keeping its own diary: every sale, every payment, every promise, written down day by day. Now comes the day the diary must become a REPORT CARD — one page answering the owner's two oldest questions: did the shop make money this year, and how much? But here's the catch: you cannot photocopy a diary and call it a report card. The stationery page says one thousand five hundred rand spent — but open the cupboard: three hundred of it is still sitting there, unused. The stock page claims three thousand one hundred — but count the shelf: two thousand eight hundred and eighty. The diary is not lying; it simply does not know what nobody has told it. So year-end has two jobs, in strict order: tidy the diary until it matches the real shop, then squeeze it into the report card. Tidy first. Squeeze second.
visual_style: A thick handwritten diary morphing page by page into a single clean report card; a cupboard door swings open to reveal unused stationery, a shelf count ticks down, two funnel-sieves pour numbers into a glowing jar.
pacing: Gentle build through the two discoveries, brisk finish on the two jobs.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the year end yourself.
